slides.headline: ALL 26 OF ELON MUSK'S NEW SATELLITES CAME ONLINE
slides.kicker: STARLINK V3 JUST SET THE NEW STANDARD.

caption:
Elon Musk just confirmed all 26 of his next-generation Starlink satellites are working.

SpaceX launched 26 Starlink V3 satellites on September 28, and every single one powered on and made contact. Musk confirmed it himself on X with one casual tweet, the way you'd check if the WiFi router is on, except his router is in orbit serving millions of people. V3 is a new generation, meaning the old version is already being left behind. Your cable company just lost more ground to a guy who owns the rockets, the satellites, and the platform he used to tell the world.

Every launch quietly takes more ground from internet providers that still need trucks, poles, and technicians to reach your door. One man now controls a growing piece of the internet above your house, no cable required. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this change means for yours.

Sources: Elon Musk on X, SpaceX

#SpaceX #Starlink #ElonMusk #Space #Technology
pinned_comment: Would you trust one person to control both your internet connection and the platform you used to find out about it? Because that is already the reality.

hook_sharpen.why: Headline [1]'s 'every single one works' is a shocking, specific outcome that lands instantly—you stop scrolling because you understand the news right now. Headline [0]'s 'over your head' requires interpretation when a 2am scroller just wants concrete impact delivered without metaphor.

editor_override: COVER IMAGE FAILS §3 ARCHETYPE LAW: The image is a plain close-up portrait of Musk against a white background — no SpaceX/Starlink brand mark, no satellite, no space context. A stranger at feed size sees a man's face and cannot guess this story is about 26 satellites going live in orbit. The correct archetype for this story is 'company/product with a famous CEO' → person + giant glossy brand mark
gate_r: s1: The photo is a dim, low-resolution candid portrait that lacks press-photo quality and is visually irrelevant to a satellite launch milestone — the slide reads better as a text-only graphic.
